content: Progestin and ethinyl estradiol are metabolized by the CYP3A4 enzyme. The co-administration of mavacamten may reduce the systemic levels of ethinyl estradiol and progestin, potentially leading to contraceptive failure or an increased risk of breakthrough bleeding. Patients should be advised to use a contraceptive method that is not influenced by CYP450 enzyme induction, such as an intrauterine system, or to add a non-hormonal contraceptive method, such as condoms, during co-administration and for four months after the last dose of mavacamten. Ethinyl estradiol can antagonize the pharmacodynamic effects of metformin, reducing its efficacy. Close monitoring is recommended when these drugs are used together. Metronidazole may decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ethinyl estradiol may reduce the efficacy of metyrapone through an unspecified interaction mechanism, potentially leading to subtherapeutic responses. Discontinuation of estrogen-containing medications, including oral contraceptives, may be advisable prior to and during metyrapone administration. Ethinyl estradiol can increase the levels or effects of mexiletine by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Ethinyl estradiol may increase the levels of midazolam by decreasing its metabolism, potentially leading to prolonged sedation. This effect is mediated through CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ethinyl estradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, increasing their serum concentrations and potentially enhancing their effects. Close monitoring is recommended. Mifepristone can reduce the effects of norethindrone acetate and ethinyl estradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Additionally, mifepristone may increase the levels of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating the avoidance of or substitution with an alternative drug. Mineral oil can decrease the levels of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents and is considered minor with unknown clinical significance. Monitoring is recommended. Minocycline may reduce the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. Mitotane can decrease the levels of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives may not be reliable during co-administration. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Avoid co-administration unless the benefits outweigh the risks. Momelotinib may increase the toxicity of ethinyl estradiol by competing for plasma protein binding. Dose adjustments of other BCRP substrates may be necessary. Close monitoring is recommended. Moxifloxacin may reduce the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. Mycophenolate may reduce the effects of ethinyl estradiol through an unknown mechanism. Patients should consider using an alternative or additional form of contraception. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. Nafcillin can decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Nelfinavir may increase the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Nemolizumab may decrease the levels of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP enzyme activity. Dosage modifications of narrow therapeutic index drugs may be necessary. Close monitoring is recommended. Neomycin may reduce the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. Nevirapine can decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives may not be reliable during co-administration. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. Nicardipine and nilotinib may increase the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Nirmatrelvir, with or without ritonavir, may decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing metabolism, possibly through CYP2C9 or CYP1A2 induction. Additional non-hormonal contraceptive methods should be considered for the remainder of the cycle. Close monitoring is recommended. Nitrofurantoin may reduce the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ethinyl estradiol may increase the serum concentrations of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) such as nortriptyline and protriptyline by reducing their oxidative metabolism. This may lead to increased antidepressant serum levels and a higher risk of TCA-related adverse effects. Close monitoring is recommended. Ofloxacin may reduce the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ethinyl estradiol may increase the levels or effects of olanzapine by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir with or without dasabuvir is contraindicated with ethinyl estradiol due to the risk of significant ALT elevations. Ethinyl estradiol-containing medications should be discontinued before initiating this hepatitis C combination regimen and restarted approximately two weeks after completing the regimen. Otesecazole, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase the effects and toxicity risks of BCRP substrates, including ethinyl estradiol. Dose adjustments of BCRP substrates may be necessary. Close monitoring is recommended. Oxcarbazepine can decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives may not be reliable during co-administration. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. Paromomycin may reduce the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. Penicillin G aqueous and penicillin VK may reduce the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora or inducing metabolism. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. Pentobarbital and phenobarbital can decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives may not be reliable during co-administration. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. Phenytoin can decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives may not be reliable during co-administration. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. Pioglitazone may decrease the levels of ethinyl estradiol through an unknown mechanism. Close monitoring is recommended. Posaconazole may increase the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Primidone can decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives may not be reliable during co-administration. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. Quinidine may increase the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. Quinupristin/dalfopristin may increase the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ethinyl estradiol may increase the levels or effects of ramelteon by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ranolazine may increase the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. Ethinyl estradiol may increase the levels or effects of rasagiline by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Repotrectinib, a CYP3A4 inducer, can decrease the levels of progestin or estrogen, potentially reducing the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. Ribociclib may increase the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifabutin can decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives may not be reliable during co-administration. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug.
